signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD records a 1W average performance of +0.839% across 4 pairs, leading the G10 board, while CHF ranks as the primary laggard at −0.424% across 6 pairs. That generates a 1.263% leader-to-laggard bilateral spread, clearing the threshold for a strong directional theme. The move is underpinned by monetary policy divergence, with RBA at 4.60% versus SNB at 0.00%, establishing a massive +460bp nominal carry advantage that widens to +337bp on an OIS basis. AUD/CHF trades at 0.5807, supported by positive cross-asset risk appetite as VIX sits at 15.0. Macro tailwinds from commodity resilience offset domestic spending cautions. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF, carry-backed bilateral momentum. Catalyst: Australia Ai Group Industry Index at 22:00 UTC. Risk: Spread compresses below 0.80% as risk sentiment reverses or equity volatility spikes.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR CFTC Leveraged Funds net positioning stands at −82,445 contracts (pctl 6, z −1.65), heavily crowded in the bottom decile of its 52-week distribution following a WoW decline of −23,640. EUR/USD spot trades at 1.1263, trapped below its SMA20 at 1.1444 and SMA50 at 1.1527. Saxo 1M implied volatility runs at 6.2% against realized HV30 of 3.9%, establishing an elevated +2.2% Vol Risk Premium. 25-delta Risk Reversal shows a persistent put skew at −0.85, signaling active hedging against further Euro depreciation despite stretched short positioning. The policy rate differential favors USD by +135bp with Fed at 4.00% versus ECB at 2.65%, reinforced by US 5Y yields adding +54bp over 20 days entirely via real yields. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, structural carry deficit meets downside options demand. Catalyst: Germany Industrial Production at 06:00 UTC. Risk: Leveraged funds cover short positions on a daily close above the SMA20 at 1.1444.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.12, positioned above its SMA20 of 156.44 while holding below the SMA200 at 158.49. A +275bp policy rate gap between Fed at 4.00% and BoJ at 1.25% sustains carry demand, yielding a +265bp differential on an OIS basis via SOFR at 3.88% versus TONA at 1.23%. Options markets reflect sharp asymmetry, where Saxo 25-delta Risk Reversal trades at an extreme put skew of −2.01 despite ATM implied volatility running at 8.4% below realized HV30 of 9.9% (VRP −1.4%). The 160.00 handle remains the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention, creating elevated tail-risk hedging in options even as spot grinds higher on carry. Cross-asset bond volatility remains elevated, with MOVE index at the 96th percentile of its trailing year versus VIX at the 12th percentile. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-driven while spot respects moving averages. Catalyst: Japan Current Account release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Spot break below SMA20 at 156.44 or verbal intervention targeting the 160.00 threshold.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Crowded Short Unwind Setup
signals.text: GBP Leveraged Funds positioning sits at net short −5,377 contracts, representing an extreme percentile reading of pctl 2 and z −2.34 across its 52-week history following a heavy 4-week liquidation of −52,881 contracts. Spot trades at 1.3274, firming intraday by +0.40% but holding beneath the descending SMA20 at 1.3354. Policy stance divergence is minimal, with Fed at 4.00% versus BoE on hold at 3.75%, leaving a narrow 25bp policy spread and a 15bp OIS edge favoring USD. However, UK 10Y yields at 5.43% offer an 11bp premium over US 10Y Treasuries at 5.32%, while 2Y spreads narrowed 7bp over the last 5 sessions. With speculative short positioning severely exhausted, cable is vulnerable to a squeeze should US dollar momentum stall. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD, short-squeeze potential against stretched CFTC positioning. Catalyst: BoE Credit Conditions Survey at 08:30 UTC. Risk: Sustained drop below intraday support at 1.3200 invalidating the base.
